name: Task Timing Planner
blurb: scheduling conflicts of periodic tasks from period and duration
intro: Simulates periodic tasks over one hyperperiod (the least common multiple of the periods) under a cooperative run-to-completion scheduler (a super loop or time-triggered scheduler) or a preemptive fixed-priority RTOS, and shows where tasks collide, how late each one starts (jitter), which deadlines are missed, and offsets that spread the tasks apart. Priority blank = rate monotonic (shorter period first).

inputs.label: Scheduler
options: Cooperative: each task runs to completion

inputs.label: Tasks
inputs.help: Times in ms. Duration = worst-case execution time. Deadline blank = the period. Priority: 0 is most urgent, blank = by period.

inputs.label: Drawing window
inputs.help: Blank: two periods of the slowest task, at most the hyperperiod.

examples.title: Super loop with a slow display task
Same tasks under a preemptive RTOS

usage: Give the scheduler (coop for run-to-completion, preempt for a fixed-priority RTOS) and a table of tasks with name, period, duration (worst-case execution time) and offset in ms, plus optional priority (0 = most urgent; blank = rate monotonic) and deadline in ms. It returns the CPU utilisation, the hyperperiod, per task the worst start delay, worst response time and deadline misses, a table of which task delayed which, suggested offsets that reduce collisions, and result.timeline (segments per task in ms) for the drawing. Use it to plan a super loop or RTOS task set, or to explain jitter.
sources: Liu & Layland, 'Scheduling algorithms for multiprogramming in a hard-real-time environment', JACM 1973 (rate monotonic, bound n(2^(1/n) - 1))
Leung & Whitehead 1982 / Audsley et al.: simulating one hyperperiod from the synchronous release is exact for fixed priorities
Michael J. Pont, 'Patterns for Time-Triggered Embedded Systems', 2001 (cooperative schedulers, task offsets)
